title: Songbook and Postcard
premise: Ines Zhou has built a career writing other people's truths, including the memoir of his rival, celebrated singer-songwriter Marisol Vega. When a postcard he mailed eleven years ago — to a lover who vanished — resurfaces in the walls of a failing bakery, it drags him back to the neighborhood, and the person, he abandoned: Theo Marchetti, the baker who never left. As Ines ghosts Marisol's book by day and repairs what he broke by night, the two projects collide when Theo's family bakery turns out to be entangled in Marisol's origin story. Ines must choose between delivering a bestseller built on borrowed lives and writing, for once, in his own name; the novel ends with him publishing under his own byline, staying past the last train, and signing a new lease beside Theo.
about_author: Noor Vasquez is a former radio archivist who spent years cataloguing listeners' letters before turning to fiction. She writes from a small apartment above a laundromat, where she collects postcards she never sends.

chapters.title: The Muscle That Lies
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ghostwriting Marisol Vega's memoir in a rented studio, Ines rehearses his creed that the heart is trainable muscle — until demolition crews gutting an old bakery find a postcard with his handwriting, eleven years stale. The beat is controlled unease cracking open.

chapters.title: Flour on the Return Ticket
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. He tracks the postcard to Marchetti & Sons Bakery, where the lease expires in ninety days, and finds Theo behind the counter — older, guarded, still keeping Ines's old coffee order. Ines lies that he's passing through. The beat is longing disguised as casualness.

chapters.title: What Marisol Won't Say
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Sharp and magnetic, Marisol dictates her rise from this same neighborhood, dodging every question about a bakery fire and a lost friend named 'T.' Ines recognizes the shape of her omissions. The beat is the thrill and rot of proximity to someone else's myth.

chapters.title: Ninety Days of Small Repairs
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Ines starts showing up after closing, fixing the espresso machine, the awning, the ledger — anything but the past. Theo lets him, testing whether presence can outrun history. A near-kiss over proofing dough ends with Theo pulling back. The beat is tentative re-earning.

chapters.title: The Fire Chapter
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Digging into Marisol's manuscript gaps, Ines learns the bakery fire eleven years ago was no accident — and that Marisol's debut song was written in its ashes about someone she loved and betrayed. His ghostwritten sentences begin to feel like theft. The beat is dread sharpening into complicity.

chapters.title: Last Train Etiquette
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo finally tells his side: the night of the fire, the letter Ines never answered, the brother who took the fall for Marisol's stolen demo tape. He asks Ines to leave before the lease does. Ines misses the last train on purpose. The beat is grief meeting stubborn hope.

chapters.title: Drafts and Confessions
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Cornered by his editor's deadline, Ines writes two manuscripts at once: Marisol's polished lie and a raw true account naming names. Marisol discovers the second draft and threatens to bury him professionally. The beat is the cost of truth made explicit.

chapters.title: The Reading at the Register
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol comes to the dying bakery incognito, hears Theo tell the fire story to a regular, and confronts the human wreckage beneath her legend. She offers Ines a deal: her version, his silence, his career intact. The beat is a villain revealed as another frightened survivor.

chapters.title: Everything the Postcard Meant
chapters.summary: Ines's POV, climax. At the lease auction, Ines publicly reads the unsent words behind the postcard and the true account of the fire, burning his ghostwriting contract in front of Marisol's lawyers. Theo learns Ines chose ruin over the deal. The beat is sacrifice as declaration.

chapters.title: Open Sign, New Lease
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, resolution. Months later: Ines's own-named book finds modest, honest readers; Marisol, unmasked but lighter, sends a postcard of apology. Theo and Ines co-sign the bakery's new lease, and Ines stays long after the last train. The beat is belonging chosen daily, not inherited.
